column2: 试药\n掌柜的递来一碗新配的汤药，说是补气血的方子。你仰头喝下，药性平和，倒无不适。掌柜满意地点点头，从柜下摸出几枚铜钱递来。
column3: Testing Medicine\nThe shopkeeper hands you a bowl of freshly prepared herbal brew, claiming it nourishes the blood and qi. You tilt your head back and drink. The medicine is mild, causing no discomfort. The shopkeeper nods with satisfaction and fishes out a few copper coins from beneath the counter, handing them to you.
Testing Medicine for Coin
Cast Off the Scholar's Robe

column2: 适逢某公忌日，长安罢市，百肆紧闭
column3: It happens to be the death anniversary of a certain dignitary. Chang'an's markets are shuttered, every shop bolted shut.
The Marketplace
Turn and Leave

column2: 里正还坐在那张磨得发亮的木凳上，像是从未挪过。你走过去的时候，他正[glitch level=6]闭着眼[/glitch]晒太阳——不，也许只是在打盹。冬天的太阳没有温度，照在他脸上像一层薄灰。
column3: The village head still sits on that wooden stool, its surface worn glossy, as if he had never moved. When you approach, he has his eyes [glitch level=6]closed[/glitch], basking in the sun — no, perhaps just dozing. The winter sun carries no warmth; it lies on his face like a thin layer of ash.

column2: 里正闭着眼，指了一个你根本不认识的方向。风里…听不到哭声了。
column3: Eyes still shut, the village head points in a direction you don't recognize at all. In the wind… you can no longer hear the crying.
The Village Head at the Entrance

column2: 我怎么对这个地方一点都不熟悉
column3: Why does this place feel so utterly unfamiliar
Turn Back to the Village Entrance

column2: 你凭着十年前的记忆在这片田野里摸索。路早就被荒草吞没了大半，但方向还在骨头里。风从奉先县城那边吹过来，夹着一股[glitch]柴̧̧̱̰̣̱̈̄̃̇́̀́̄烟̄̂̈̆̂̇̌̀[/glitch]味。
column3: You grope through the fields, relying on memories from a decade ago. The path has long been swallowed by wild grass, but its direction still lives in your bones. The wind blows over from Fengxian county town, carrying a whiff of [glitch]f̈̄̃̇í̀́̄ŗ̧̱̰̣̱ē̂̈̆̂̇̌̀ẅ̄̃̇́̀́̄o̧̧̱̰̣̱ō̂̈̆̂̇̌̀d[/glitch] smoke.

column2: 远处的茅草屋里传来婴儿断断续续的啼哭，像是在硬撑。
column3: From a distant thatched hut comes the intermittent cry of a baby, as if struggling to hold on.
A Familiar Path

column2: 你回到村头，察看着四周
column3: You return to the village entrance and survey your surroundings
Step Back Outside

column2: 门虚掩着。你推开门，屋里的霉味混着一股甜腻的腐烂气息迎面扑来。地上趴着一具[glitch level=4]干尸[/glitch]——骨节粗大，肩宽，不像女人，更不是孩子。你蹲下来翻看尸体的手，指节上有老茧，是握锄头的痕迹。
column3: The door is ajar. You push it open. A musty odor mixed with a cloying sweetness of decay hits your face. On the floor lies a [glitch level=4]desiccated corpse[/glitch] — thick-knuckled, broad-shouldered. Not a woman, certainly not a child. You crouch down and turn over the hand. Calloused knuckles. The marks of a hoe.

column2: 你急疯了，在泥水里跌跌撞撞。那阵哭声变得极其微弱，几乎要被风声盖过。
column3: Mad with desperation, you stumble through the mud. The crying has grown terribly faint, nearly swallowed by the wind.
The Old Home
The crying grows weaker…

column2: 你站在奉先村的村口，风从骊山方向灌过来，把衣摆吹得猎猎作响。十年前的记忆在脑子里乱撞，每条巷子都像，又都不像。村口的老槐树还在，但树下的石凳上坐着陌生的人。
column3: You stand at the entrance of Fengxian village. The wind barrels in from the direction of Mount Li, whipping your robes with a snapping sound. Memories from ten years ago crash through your mind — every alley looks right and wrong at the same time. The old locust tree at the entrance still stands, but strangers now sit on the stone bench beneath it.
You don't know where home is

column2: 你又站在了村口。风还是从骊山方向来，但现在你知道有些东西已经不一样了。里正死了，那片你住过的区域已经换了模样——他们似乎搬迁到了你不熟悉的地方。你不常回来，也没钱，这些年村子对你来说，已经成了一个陌生的地方。
column3: You stand at the village entrance again. The wind still comes from Mount Li, but now you know — some things are no longer the same. The village head is dead. The area where you once lived has changed beyond recognition — they seem to have relocated somewhere unfamiliar. You rarely come back, and you have no money. Over the years, the village has become a foreign place to you.

column2: 文思枯涩，笔端如坠千钧，纸上空无一字
column3: Your literary thoughts run dry and coarse. The brush-tip feels weighed down by a thousand pounds. The paper remains blank — not a single word.
Summoned to Court
Begin the Examination

column2: 你带着这几年在长安四处干谒换来的微薄名望，深吸一口气，跨过贡院高高的门槛。阳光洒在你的白袍上，你觉得大唐的未来就在你笔下。
column3: Carrying the meager reputation you've scraped together from years of petitioning officials across Chang'an, you draw a deep breath and step over the Examination Hall's towering threshold. Sunlight falls upon your white robes. You feel that the future of the Great Tang lies beneath your brush.
Enter the Examination Hall
Choose A
A Standard Poetry Question
Question One

column2: 针砭时弊：言明边镇兵权过重，朝堂言路闭塞。
column3: Criticize the current abuses: Argue that border garrisons hold excessive military power and the court has stifled all channels of honest counsel.

column2: 违心作答：“右相调理阴阳，海内晏清，真乃千古贤相！”
column3: Answer against your conscience: "The Grand Chancellor harmonizes yin and yang; the realm is at peace under his governance. Truly a sage minister for the ages!"

column2: 考官死死盯着你的笔尖。你敢写下半个字，今天就别想活着走出贡院。
column3: The examiner fixes his stare on the tip of your brush. Write so much as half a character of dissent, and you won't leave this examination hall alive today.
A wave of nausea rises in your stomach

column2: 试卷的第二题并非诗词经义，而是策问：“今圣上垂拱而治，右相理政，天下如何？”你握紧了笔，冷汗滴在纸上。主考官（李林甫的心腹）在走道里来回巡视，眼神阴冷。
column3: The second question on the exam paper is not about poetry or the classics — it's a policy essay: "His Majesty governs through effortless virtue while the Grand Chancellor administers the realm. How fares the empire?" You grip your brush tighter; cold sweat drips onto the paper. The chief examiner — Li Linfu's trusted man — paces the aisles, his gaze dark and cold.
Question Two

column2: 天宝六年，贡院放榜。你满怀信心地挤入人群，寻找自己的名字。
column3: In the sixth year of Tianbao, the Examination Hall posts its results. Full of confidence, you squeeze into the crowd, searching for your name.

column2: 没有。不仅没有你，你认识的所有才子，郑虔、高适……全都不在榜上.
column3: Nothing. Not just you — every talented scholar you know — Zheng Qian, Gao Shi… none of them are on the list.

column2: 相国李林甫上表贺皇帝：‘天下英才尽入彀中，野无遗贤。’

column2: 宴席之上，玉盘珍馐，觥筹交错。你端着酒杯在人群中穿梭，试图与几位说得上话的人物攀谈。然而这些贵人要么被更显赫的宾客包围，要么对你只是敷衍地点头寒暄便转身而去。夜深宴散，朱门在身后吱呀关上。你立在阶下，望着一地狼藉的残烛，心中空落落的。这重金购得的入席券，终究没有换来一句承诺。
column3: At the banquet, jade platters bear rare delicacies, wine cups cross in festive toasts. You navigate through the crowd, cup in hand, attempting to strike up conversation with several figures of influence. Yet these dignitaries are either surrounded by more prominent guests or merely offer you a perfunctory nod before turning away. Night deepens; the feast disperses. The vermilion gates creak shut behind you. Standing beneath the steps, gazing at the scattered remains of spent candles, emptiness fills your chest. The seat at this table, bought at great cost, has yielded not a single promise.
The Feast Ends — The Guests Vanish
